Implementation details per topic

core

Responsibility
Cross-topic plumbing: error codes and exceptions, the command wrapper for WebSocket commands, reply and error factories, id generation, shared helpers and the protocols that let topics use each other without importing.
Key classes
ErrorCode and the TdcError family (core.errors), tdc_command (core.command), ErrorFactory, ResponseFactory, HasReplies and the other narrow protocols (core.protocols). The runtime data lives in the root modules data (TdcData, get_data) and bootstrap (build_data).
Data flow
async_setup_entry calls build_data, which creates every factory and manager once and wires them with constructor arguments; the result is stored in hass.data[DOMAIN] and fetched by get_data(hass). A command arrives at HA's websocket_api, passes the schema and require_admin, runs the handler inside tdc_command and is answered by ResponseFactory; any exception becomes a TdcError through ErrorFactory and is logged once with its code.
Notable decisions
core is a leaf package: it imports no topic. The composition root is the root module bootstrap, the only place that knows all concrete classes; data holds the runtime data and the service locator get_data(hass). The only except Exception is in core.command. Translation keys are the lower-case enum member names.
Modules
core, core.command, core.error_factory, core.errors, core.hashing, core.ids, core.keys, core.labels, core.limits, core.protocols, core.response_factory, core.targets

devices

Responsibility
Creating generated devices from a creation job, changing their area or curve, and finding who uses a device.
Key classes
DevicesManager, CreationJob, SignalEditor, DeviceUsage; entity_id_of resolves an entity id for the native or the MQTT unique id.
Data flow
create request -> job_from_request -> DevicesManager.async_create: resolve template, check limits, reserve device numbers in the store, distribute areas, let DeviceFactory build DeviceDefs, then in chunks of 25 per device adapter.create + store + adapter.announce and a yield to the loop; the store is saved in a finally so a failed job keeps what exists.
Notable decisions
The store keeps plain dicts; every read builds fresh dataclasses (store.devices() is O(N)). Limits live in const.py. Area names are created through AreaAssigner which records only areas it created itself.
Modules
devices, devices.filters, devices.manager, devices.schema, devices.signal_editor, devices.usage, devices.view

templates

Responsibility
Bundled and user YAML templates, their voluptuous schemas, validation of entity definitions and the creation of DeviceDef objects from a template.
Key classes
TemplateRegistry (loads bundled/*.yaml and <config>/hass_test_data_creator/templates/*.yaml in the executor: bundled files with load_yaml_dict, user files with yaml.safe_load), TemplateFactory, Template, DeviceFactory.
Data flow
YAML -> TEMPLATE_SCHEMA -> TemplateFactory.entity (ENTITY_SCHEMA + content checks per platform) -> Template. A custom job builds a template from request dicts through the same factory.
Notable decisions
A user file with the same id replaces a bundled one; an invalid bundled file raises TPL_INVALID and stops setup, while a user file that is invalid, a link, too large or unreadable is skipped with a warning (at most 200 files of 256 KiB, read with yaml.safe_load). Device seeds are crc32(seed:template:index), so they are stable across runs.
Modules
templates, templates.device_factory, templates.factory, templates.registry, templates.schema

engine

Responsibility
Pure signal functions, the clock with time lapse, the tick, and the behaviours (state and logic of one entity, independent of the output).
Key classes
SignalSpec + value_at (pure functions of time and seed, SplitMix64 hash), SignalFactory, Clock, Tick, Behaviour and its subclasses, BehaviourFactory.
Data flow
Tick fires one dispatcher signal per interval. Each native sensor/climate entity and each MQTT runtime is connected to it; they call behaviour.tick(now), which returns whether the value changed, and write HA state or publish.
Notable decisions
Behaviours know only a Scheduler protocol (now, at, call_later), so native and MQTT outputs share them. Signal time is the local wall clock in seconds so daily curves follow the day; the clock base is reset on every start when time lapse is above 1.
Modules
engine, engine.behaviour_factory, engine.behaviours, engine.clock, engine.signal_factory, engine.signals, engine.tick

faults

Responsibility
Describes the faults that can be injected on an entity for a limited time.
Key classes
FaultFactory (spec table per kind, voluptuous schema per kind), Fault (frozen dataclass with flags: unavailable, frozen, transform, message delay/repeats).
Data flow
An action named fault_<kind> is resolved by ActionFactory to a closure that calls FaultFactory.create and behaviour.start_fault; the behaviour arms a timer that ends the fault.
Notable decisions
The fault only carries data; behaviours and the MQTT runtime interpret it. FaultFactory.create still branches on the kind to build the object (inside the factory, as the rules allow).
Modules
faults, faults.factory

scheduler

Responsibility
Actions on entities, triggers, planning of runs per day and firing them with a single timer.
Key classes
ActionFactory (table of (platform, action) -> coroutine), ActionRunner, TriggerFactory + Trigger subclasses, SchedulePlanner, ScheduleManager.
Data flow
ScheduleManager._replan asks the planner for all runs of the rest of today, keeps them in a sorted list and arms async_track_point_in_utc_time for the first. _fire executes all due runs, then re-arms. A midnight listener replans. A run resolves the target (devices_for) and calls ActionRunner.async_run_on for each device.
Notable decisions
Times of a day are drawn from crc32(seed:schedule id:date) so the same seed gives the same day, also after a restart. Failures of single devices are audited and do not stop the run; non-TdcError exceptions are not caught in _fire.
Modules
scheduler, scheduler.actions, scheduler.manager, scheduler.planner, scheduler.runner, scheduler.schema, scheduler.triggers

scenarios

Responsibility
Named lists of steps with relative delays.
Key classes
ScenarioManager, STEP_SCHEMA/SCENARIO_FIELDS.
Data flow
async_run accumulates after_s; a step with zero delay runs at once, others get an async_call_later timer that is tracked in a set and cancelled on unload.
Notable decisions
Steps reuse ActionRunner; a scenario can be started by a schedule (ScheduleManager depends on ScenarioManager).
Modules
scenarios, scenarios.manager, scenarios.schema

outputs

Responsibility
Turns device descriptions into Home Assistant objects (native), MQTT discovery messages, or a Zigbee2MQTT bridge emulation.
Key classes
OutputAdapterFactory and OutputAdapter, NativeAdapter, MqttAdapter; BehaviourRuntime (base) with MqttDevices and Z2mDevices; MqttProfileFactory/Z2mProfileFactory (one profile per platform); Z2mPayloadFactory; MqttClient.
Data flow
MQTT outputs start behaviours themselves, subscribe to the command wildcard, follow the tick and publish through MqttClient.async_publish, which records every retained topic in the store. Z2M publishes one JSON state per device (coalesced with _pending), bridge topics and group states. The late fault holds messages back with timers; duplicate repeats them.
Notable decisions
Z2M refuses a foreign retained bridge/state and the default zigbee2mqtt topic without confirmation. Retained topics are cleaned up from the recorded list only. Device and group names that become Zigbee2MQTT topics are checked by outputs.z2m.names.is_friendly_name (one topic level, not bridge).
Modules
outputs, outputs.adapter, outputs.base, outputs.mqtt, outputs.mqtt.adapter, outputs.mqtt.client, outputs.mqtt.devices, outputs.mqtt.labels, outputs.mqtt.profiles, outputs.mqtt.runtime, outputs.native, outputs.native.adapter, outputs.profile_factory, outputs.z2m, outputs.z2m.devices, outputs.z2m.names, outputs.z2m.payloads, outputs.z2m.profiles

platforms

Responsibility
Native Home Assistant entity classes (thin shells around behaviours).
Key classes
TdcEntity mixin, TdcSensor, TdcSwitch, TdcLight, TdcCover, TdcClimate, EntityFactory, HassScheduler, platform_setup.
Data flow
Each platform module (sensor.py ...) calls platform_setup; stored devices are added at setup and new ones through the SIGNAL_DEVICES_ADDED dispatcher signal. Entities register their behaviour in the shared live dict so actions can find it.
Notable decisions
State survives restart through RestoreEntity for switches, lights, covers and thermostats. Every sensor and climate entity has its own dispatcher subscription to the tick.
Modules
platforms, platforms.actuators, platforms.entities, platforms.factory, platforms.scheduler, platforms.setup

history

Responsibility
Writes hourly long-term statistics for the past days and remembers which statistic ids it created.
Key classes
HistoryManager, SeriesFactory (+ Series), StatisticsClient.
Data flow
Request -> _targets (sensors with a state class) -> limit check against MAX_HISTORY_ROWS -> _build in the executor (12 samples per hour from the same signal functions) -> async_import_statistics per series on the loop -> ids stored in created_statistics.
Notable decisions
Counters start at the beginning of the history so that consumption is visible in the past. Everything is built in one executor job before any row is written.
Modules
history, history.factory, history.manager, history.recorder, history.schema

removal

Responsibility
Plans and runs the removal of everything the integration created, and cleans up when the config entry is deleted.
Key classes
RemovalPlanner + RemovalPlan, RemovalRunner + Forgetters, async_cleanup_after_entry_removal.
Data flow
plan reads the store (devices, runs, topics, statistics, created areas) and the device registry (orphans of this config entry). RemovalRunner.async_run refuses used devices, checks that MQTT and recorder are available if needed, forgets schedules/scenarios/groups, removes devices through their adapter, clears retained topics and statistics, deletes empty created areas and saves.
Notable decisions
Only ids recorded in the store or devices carrying this config entry are touched; areas are deleted only if the integration created them and they are empty. Retained topics are cleared last, when nothing publishes any more.
Modules
removal, removal.cleanup, removal.orphans, removal.planner, removal.runner

store

Responsibility
Persistence in one Home Assistant Store (key hass_test_data_creator.data, version 1).
Key classes
TdcStore: dicts of devices, runs, schedules, scenarios, groups, published topics, created statistics, created areas and counters.
Data flow
Reads build dataclasses from dicts on every call; writes replace the dict entry. User changes call async_save at once, retained-topic bookkeeping uses async_delay_save (5 s).
Notable decisions
No secrets. No migration function yet (version 1). Loaded data is merged over an empty skeleton without validation.
Modules
store, store.migrate, store.store

api

Responsibility
The hass_test_data_creator/* WebSocket commands.
Key classes
Only handler functions decorated with @tdc_command; COMMANDS lists them for registration.
Data flow
Handler -> get_data(hass) -> topic manager -> plain dict reply. Services in services.py mirror most commands.
Notable decisions
devices/list builds its reply (entity states, usage) in the handler; removal/run plans and runs in one call.
Modules
api, api.bulk, api.devices, api.groups, api.history, api.info, api.removal, api.scenarios, api.schedules, api.transfer

groups

Responsibility
Groups of Zigbee2MQTT devices.
Key classes
GroupManager.
Data flow
Add/update validate members and name, store the group, save, then tell Z2mDevices to republish the bridge groups and group states.
Notable decisions
Group numbers come from a counter in the store; the name cannot contain a slash or be bridge.
Modules
groups, groups.manager, groups.schema

areas

Responsibility
Distribution of devices over area names and creation/cleanup of areas.
Key classes
AreaAssigner, distribute.
Data flow
distribute returns one area name per device (even or seeded random); ensure finds or creates the area and records it when created.
Notable decisions
An existing area with the same name is reused and never deleted later.
Modules
areas, areas.assigner, areas.distribution

audit

Responsibility
The only place that logs actions.
Key classes
AuditEntryFactory, AuditEntry, AuditLog, format_value.
Data flow
A manager records an entry from the factory; AuditLog.record formats every field with format_value (single line, quoted, 120 characters).
Notable decisions
Entries are created per kind of action in one factory.
Modules
audit, audit.factory, audit.log

panel

Responsibility
The Lit/TypeScript sidebar panel (panel-src/src), built to one ES module in frontend/.
Key classes
TdcPanel (tabs, badge), TdcElement (base: hass, api, tr), TdcPollingElement (10 s refresh), TdcApi (typed WebSocket client), forms and panels per topic.
Data flow
A tab element loads info and templates on connect, polls its list every 10 s, and calls TdcApi methods that map one to one to backend commands. Components talk through DOM events (tdc-*).
Notable decisions
Texts only through i18n (English and German tables, the German one typed as Record<TextKey, string>), colours from HA CSS variables; no unsafeHTML.
Files
see the panel section
